name: My Son
provinceNote: My Son is now inside Da Nang city after the Quang Nam merger.
dotReason: Worth it if you are already nearby
summary: My Son is a valley of Cham temple towers west of Hoi An, built between the 4th and 13th centuries. War damage is obvious. Go in the morning, with a guide or the site notes, if you want the ruins to mean more than a photograph.
timeNeeded: Half a day from Hoi An
fee: Site ticket; confirm at the entrance
getThere: About 45–60 minutes by road from Hoi An
seoTitle: My Son sanctuary — hours, tickets, and how to get there
seoDescription: How to visit the Cham towers at My Son from Hoi An, and whether the half-day is worth it.
intro: The temples are brick towers in a forested valley, sacred to the Cham kings. Many were damaged in the twentieth century. What remains is still the most important Cham site you can reach from Hoi An.
Tours leave Hoi An early because the valley gets hot. A private car lets you leave when the ticket gate opens. There is a small museum at the entrance; read it before the walk.
gettingAround: You cannot walk here from Hoi An. Car, taxi, or tour bus are the options. Electric carts or a walk cover the last stretch from the visitor center to the towers.

stayAreas.name: Hoi An
stayAreas.summary: Sleep in Hoi An and come out for the morning.

eat: Eat in Hoi An. The site has basic drinks, not a meal worth planning around.
interestsBody: History and brick architecture. Skip it if you have no interest in ruins and would rather have a second day in the old town.

faqs.a: Yes if you want the Cham context for central Vietnam. No if you are collecting viewpoints. The valley is quiet and damaged, not monumental in the way Angkor is.
